subject: Partner metering integration: evidence shim for marketplace listing
messages:
From: Devon Lowe <devon@acmedata.com>

Cc: Marketplace Ops <marketplace-ops@aws-partners.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace metering evidence — need a 'shim' for usage proof

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the quick tour of Redwood Dedicated last week — the team loved the performance numbers. We're progressing toward an AWS Marketplace listing but hit a snag on the metering/evidence side. AWS wants an itemized usage record (S3-style CSV) and a lightweight verification endpoint for each billing cycle.

Our engineering lead suggested we could use a small "metering shim" that maps our internal usage keys to AWS-metering events and emits a signed CSV. Do you have a recommended pattern or example for how Redwood typically surfaces metering evidence for co-sell listings?

Attached a sample of our internal usage report for Q3. Would appreciate a quick run-through of what we should hand to Marketplace Ops to avoid a rejection.

Thanks,
Devon
Head of Partnerships
AcmeData Inc.

Subject: Re: Marketplace metering evidence — need a 'shim' for usage proof

Devon —

Short answer: yes, we do this frequently. Long answer: we have a lightweight pattern we call the "metering shim" that sits on the partner side but follows a predictable schema and signed envelope so Marketplace/Platform teams can validate ingestion. I'll loop Ben for the technical spec and Vanessa for commercial / revshare implications.

High-level next steps:
- Ben: confirm minimal CSV schema and an example signed envelope (public key + signature).
- Devon: confirm cadence (daily vs. per-invoice) and whether you can expose an HTTPS endpoint for signature verification.
- Vanessa: we should propose a simple revshare split and a DocuSign agreement to capture marketplace entitlements.

I'll hold here for Ben's spec. If you want a call, I can do 30 minutes Monday.

—Karthik
Sr. Manager, Cloud Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Devon Lowe <devon@acmedata.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 13:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace metering evidence — need a 'shim' for usage proof

Devon, Karthik —

Attaching a short spec and a sample signed CSV output. Key points from an ops/engineering perspective:

- Schema: timestamp_iso, customer_id, product_sku, tokens_used, cost_cents, signature
- Signature: HMAC-SHA256 using a rotating key; we recommend publishing the key fingerprint and a verification endpoint.
- Cadence: daily aggregates are fine for Marketplace; per-invoice will take longer to validate. Daily CSV + per-invoice reconciliation works well.
- Storage: S3 with a lifecycle (30d hot, 365d cold) is normal. Provide a presigned URL for market ops ingestion.

Stub attachments included: redwood-metering-shim-spec.pdf and an example CSV.

Quick note on security: we can provide a sample verification endpoint (stateless) that checks signature + schema and returns a 200/400 with a short JSON body. If Marketplace Ops insists on a signed artifact rather than an endpoint, we can provide a signed bundle (zip + .sig).

Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood-metering-shim-spec.pdf (PDF, 92KB)]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Devon Lowe <devon@acmedata.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 08:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace metering evidence — need a 'shim' for usage proof

Devon —

Thanks Ben, this is exactly the level of detail Marketplace Ops wants. From Redwood's commercial side, a couple quick asks before we publish:

- Revshare: propose 85/15 in favor of the publisher (AcmeData 85 / Redwood 15) for the first 12 months while you ramp. Open to different splits if you bring >$250k ARR in year 1.
- Billing flow: confirm whether AcmeData will invoice Redwood or Redwood will collect via Marketplace and reconcile. We prefer Marketplace collection with monthly remittance.
- Agreement: I'll send revshare + entitlement language; can you confirm the legal entity and signatory?

If those items look good, I'll prepare the DocuSign envelope and loop Finance.

—Vanessa
Head of Partnerships, Commercial
Redwood Inference
